transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-02-19 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: Zoom (internal)
Attendees: Lena (AE), Marcus (SE), Diego (CSM), Priya (Product), Morgan (role-play buyer), Taylor (role-play CTO), Jamie (role-play ML)

Summary: internal SE enablement — focus on concise messaging, competitive positioning vs Anthropic/OpenAI, and two demo rehearsals (12-min full and 8-min quick). Role-play with interruption patterns and objection handling.

Topics: messaging pillars, 12-min demo flow, 8-min elevator demo, latency/cost tradeoff script, security/compliance quick answers, competitive rebuttals, next steps

00:00 Lena: okay everyone thanks for joining, this is the Champion Lab practice run, we're doing two rehearsals, first a full 12 minute flow then an 8 minute elevator. Marcus are you good to lead the tech demo on the first run
00:28 Marcus: yep, I'll start with a short architecture slide then jump to a live run — note: we're using a pre-warmed dedicated pool emu for the recording so latency looks optimistic, call that out, we don't want customers to expect the same on cold starts
01:05 Morgan (buyer): quick question, what's the single biggest delta between Redwood and Bedrock for us as a product team?
01:22 Lena: good, prioritize: predictable SLOs and cost controls, so customers can plan unit economics. Bedrock is a broad service but it mixes model variants and you end up building routing yourself. Bedford? bedrock? (laugh) sorry, speech slip — but main point is predictable latency and routing policies
01:47 Marcus: and from SE side, runtime optimizations — continuous batching and KV cache savings for chat workloads, that tends to beat vanilla hosted endpoints on tokens per dollar in our internal benchmarks
02:10 Taylor (CTO): are you saying caching could break context for some prompts? we've seen weird cache bleed in other vendors
02:25 Marcus: great callout, yes it's about prefix safety and policy — we recommend per-route cache keys, we show customers how to scope caches by session id and user intent, and we have guardrails to invalidate at rollout. we'll show an example in the demo
03:00 Lena: ok demo script note — open with customer pain, then numbers: 30% token cost reduction example, 40% latency improvement in our demo cluster, then show the failover routing to cheaper model when dedicated hits threshold
03:28 Jamie (ML Eng): can you clarify the 30% number — is that from quantization only or batching plus cache?
03:40 Marcus: it's combined — typical stack: 8-bit quantization plus intelligent batching and prefix cache reuse. in our benchmark spreadsheet we break it down, i'll attach, it's not a promise but a realistic observed delta on customer workloads
04:12 Diego: for objections — when buyers ask about model fidelity vs quantization, recommended line: "We offer validated quantization profiles per model and per workload; we run evals on your prompt set; if quality degradation is detected we rollback or route to a full-precision variant"
04:45 Morgan (buyer): role-play: we ask: "how do you compare to OpenAI?"
04:52 Lena: short answer: OpenAI is a model-first API, we are an inference-first platform — easier to predict costs and run in VPC/dedicated modes. then fallback: mention streaming and tool calls parity
05:20 Marcus: add that we have per-token cost visibility in the Console which helps engineering prioritize prompts, that's a good tangible benefit for product teams
05:46 Lena: good interruption — now demo run 1 start, Marcus take us through the 12-min flow. note: pretend customer data residency requirement is EU only
06:12 Marcus: starting architecture slide, single region EU cluster, dedicated pool with autoscale and burst, show route policy config — here i'm going to the console... (typing noises) — ok switching to live run, launching a chat session, prefix cache warmed for user history
07:05 Marcus: live query: "summarize last 10 customer interactions and suggest churn risk actions" — generating... response arrives, latency 180ms token streaming (note: internal test env), response shows extraction of entities and recommended outreach steps
07:45 Jamie (role-play ML): interruption: the output looks canned, where's the customization?
07:57 Marcus: good, show prompt template editing, show tool-calls to CRM, show structured output JSON that maps to our webhook. (jamble of words) the transcription might show some glitches, but we'd call out the mapping to downstream actions
08:40 Taylor (CTO): security check — what keys are stored where and how do we integrate with KMS?
08:56 Marcus: we support customer-managed keys via KMS or HSM, logs are stored in the private control plane for Private deployments, and audit logs are available with retention config — refer to security one-pager we link at the end
09:30 Lena: role-play objection: "we already use Anthropic for chat, why switch?"
09:38 Marcus: pragmatic: Anthropic has strong safety but if your goal is operational predictability and multi-env deployment (hosted, dedicated, private) Redwood reduces ops burden and gives cost levers — cite case study X for migration example (we'll attach doc)
10:05 Morgan (buyer): counter: "but Anthropic quality is better for safety focused prompts"
10:15 Lena: acknowledge: yes for some safety tasks Anthropic is strong; our playbook is to measure on customer's prompts and show tradeoffs, and to propose hybrid routing (sensitive prompts route to SAFER model)
10:38 Marcus: demo continue — show rollout: canary to 5% traffic then auto-rollback on quality regressions. show trace that flags regression by prompt set. (note: a few stutters here)
11:30 Marcus: finishing demo, switch to short 8-min elevator demo plan — cut architecture, go straight to 3 user stories, one-liners for performance and cost, closing ask: run pilot with 1-week dedicated pool
12:05 Lena: practice role-play close: "If it sounds reasonable, we'd propose a 4-week pilot on a small dedicated pool with your EU data residency, we will run evals on your prompt set and provide a cost estimate and quality report by week two"
12:32 Morgan (buyer): pause — what about SLA and uptime for a pilot?
12:40 Diego: pilots include baseline SLOs, for enterprise Dedicated we have SLA options; we'll put SLA guidance in the pilot agreement and escalate via CSM if they want production SLAs
13:05 Priya (Product): note on messaging — avoid saying "we're faster" without context; prefer "we deliver predictable latency SLOs and controls to tune cost/latency tradeoffs"
13:30 Lena: ok encore role-play: Marcus you'll do 8-min elevator. I'll play the buyer and throw two quick objections mid-demo to test interruption handling
14:00 Marcus: starting elevator demo... (fast cut) show quick summary: problem statement, tech differentiator, two slides of proof points, live sample request, closing ask — generate a sample answer in 90s
15:10 Lena (buyer): objection 1: "How do you handle peak traffic spikes?"
15:18 Marcus: autoscale burst capacity plus routing to cheaper variants, plus pre-warmed reserved slots — also the recommend design is to set fallback policies for degraded performance to maintain availability
15:45 Lena (buyer): objection 2: "Are logs sent to third parties?"
15:53 Marcus: no, logs remain in the control plane unless customer opts into external integrations; for Private we support on-prem log forwarding, for Hosted we retain per-customer logs with retention policy
16:20 Jamie (role-play ML): small note, the generated sample missed an entity — shows model hallucination in an edge case. Marcus: yeah we'll call out evaluation process to detect hallucinations and tie to rollout gates
16:50 Diego: feedback round — structure: great pacing, Marcus talk slower at the part where you edit prompt templates so customers see the mapping, Lena: your role-play interruptions were realistic but try not to stack two objections back-to-back, it confuses SE
17:20 Priya: messaging tweak — replace "token savings" with "expected cost delta" when talking to finance folks, and have a single slide with three finance-friendly bullets
17:46 Lena: ok now quick mock Q&A for security/compliance: Morgan asks about SOC2 scope, Marcus answer?
18:00 Marcus: we are SOC 2 Type II in our Hosted control plane, Dedicated includes audit logs and optional SOC coverage in the contract; for Private we provide artifact templates we can share. reference: security deck link https://redwood.internal/security/pilot-sheets (internal)
18:40 Morgan: role-play: procurement asks for vendor questionnaire — who owns completion?
18:48 Diego: CSM owns initial response, legal can step in for bespoke asks; we'll ask customer to raise the security questionnaire early in the pilot
19:10 Lena: timing check — we've covered the two demos and main objections, last 10 minutes for artifact review and recording notes. Marcus please flag which clips you want us to keep for the enablement library
19:30 Marcus: list: 8-min elevator clip, 90s tool-call snippet, 3-min security Q&A. i'll mark timestamps in the recording and extract clips
20:00 Lena: let's do lightning round of rebuttals — i'll read objection, you respond quickly
20:10 Lena: "We already have a data residency contract with cloud provider"
20:14 Marcus: "We can deploy Private with same residency and integrate your KMS — no data leaves your VPC by default"
20:25 Lena: "Quantization reduces quality"
20:28 Marcus: "We run per-prompt-set evals and allow routing to full-precision variants if regression appears"
20:38 Lena: "Costs sound complex"
20:40 Diego: "We provide per-token cost dashboards and recommended batching/quant profiles to hit target cost numbers"
21:00 Priya: quick doc references — attach: condensed demo script (link: https://redwood.app/decks/champion-lab-v2.pdf), competitive playbook snippet, pilot checklist in Confluence
21:20 Lena: closing notes: we'll implement the edits: shorten intro, emphasize predictable SLOs, and prepare three short clips for enablement library. next steps and action items as noted. big thanks, practice was high value
